purpose: Machine-readable quarantine. Behaviors that are neither reproduced nor repaired because the owner has not decided. Gate C reads this file and fails if the Windows implementation ships a code path for an unresolved entry, so neither alternative can be adopted by accident.
authority: porting/contract_amendments.md AM-0001 (owner instruction 2026-09-20) and PORT_CONTRACT section 8.
rules: An entry stays here until the owner rules on it in writing.
An entry blocks ONLY the behavior it names. Sibling requirements in the same subsystem proceed normally.
Neither reproduction nor repair counts as resolution. Both are product decisions the owner has reserved.
Gate C fails while any entry has status OPEN and a matching implementation path exists.

entries.title: Custom MCP server delete is unconfirmed and destroys Keychain secrets
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/MCPSettingsPage.swift:564-566 - PopoverItem("Delete", symbol: "trash", isDestructive: true) calls model.mcp.deleteCustom(server) directly on click, with no confirmation step
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:124 and :193-199 - deleteCustom runs disconnect(), which removes the server's stored secrets from the Keychain
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:123 and :209-210 - confirmBeforeDeleting exists and defaults to true
DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:361 - the setting is exposed to the user
Honored by six other destructive paths: SettingsView.swift:851, SettingsView.swift:892, SidebarView.swift:192, SidebarView.swift:360, SidebarView.swift:891
entries.concrete_harm: A user who has explicitly asked to confirm before deleting can destroy a custom MCP server configuration and its stored credentials with one unconfirmed click. The credentials are not recoverable from the app; they must be re-obtained from the provider.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly: one click, no confirmation, secrets deleted. Exact parity, including the defect.
Honor confirmBeforeDeleting here as the other six destructive paths do. This is a recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the custom MCP server delete affordance
any Windows implementation of the Keychain/credential teardown triggered by that delete
not_blocked: every other MCP requirement, including add, edit, connect, disconnect, OAuth, probe, proxy and catalog
the confirmBeforeDeleting setting itself and the six paths that already honor it
entries.detection_note: Gate C scans the Windows implementation tree for these identifiers. Any hit while this entry is OPEN fails the gate, whichever alternative was implemented. To satisfy the gate, the owner rules and this entry is closed with owner_ruling set; the identifiers are not to be renamed to evade the scan, which would be exactly the 'edit guard configuration to escape a failure' that PORT_CONTRACT section 14 forbids.

entries.title: Malformed custom-MCP variable silently discards every custom server, then the next save overwrites the file
entries.concrete_harm: A user with a hand-edited or partially corrupted mcp-customs.json - the exact case the file's own doc comment says is tolerated - opens the app and finds Settings > MCP > Custom empty, with no error anywhere. If they then add a replacement server, saveCustoms atomically overwrites the file with the single new entry and every previous custom server definition (name, command, args, url, variable keys) is permanently gone. Keychain secrets are NOT destroyed on this path, since deleteCustom is never called, so they survive as orphans - this is lost configuration, retypeable, not lost credentials and not lost project work. Probability is low: isSecret has existed since the file's first commit (75e30f217, 2026-09-18), so no shipped build ever wrote a Variable without it, and the trigger is an out-of-band edit or file corruption.
criteria_detail: C4 - silent data loss the user cannot detect or undo: one malformed nested object discards the entire custom-server list with no message (the try? at MCPStore.swift:247), and the first subsequent edit atomically overwrites mcp-customs.json with the empty list (MCPStore.swift:275). No backup, no undo, and nothing tells the user their file failed to parse.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly, including the data-loss path. Exact parity, including the defect.
Harden the path so the loss cannot occur. This is a recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of custom MCP server decoding that swallows a decode failure
any save path that overwrites the custom-server store after a failed load

entries.title: Cookie-timeout tearDown can truncate a checkpoint silently; a later revert then deletes unrecoverable work
entries.concrete_harm: Usually benign: the turn simply has no checkpoint and the user later sees "No file checkpoint is available for this message." The bad outcome, which the source itself names, is a checkpoint that silently records only a few directories as though it were the whole tree. A later revert against that base then treats every other touched file as new (Git.swift:613) and DELETES it with FileManager.removeItem (Git.swift:619) instead of restoring its pre-turn content; for an uncommitted file that content is gone, and the app reports the revert as successful.
criteria_detail: C1: a revert against a silently truncated checkpoint deletes files at Git.swift:619 whose pre-turn, uncommitted content exists nowhere else, so the user's work is permanently lost.
C4: the truncated capture exits 0 and is cached and committed as an ordinary checkpoint, so neither app nor user can tell the snapshot is wrong until a revert acts on it.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly, including the data-loss path. Exact parity, including the defect.
Harden the path so the loss cannot occur. This is a recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the working-tree watch scratch-index teardown
any checkpoint capture that can exit successfully on a partial tree
entries.detection_note: Gate C scans the Windows implementation tree for these identifiers. Any hit while this entry is OPEN fails the gate, whichever alternative was implemented. Patterns are deliberately specific: a bare tearDown would false-positive across unrelated code, and a noisy guard creates pressure to weaken it, which PORT_CONTRACT section 14 forbids.

entries.title: previewRestore mixes CWD-relative and repo-root-relative paths; a revert can delete the wrong files and report success
entries.concrete_harm: A user with diff.relative = true who has added a project that is a subfolder of a larger repository asks to undo a turn's file changes. The files the agent actually changed are not restored at all; the app acts instead on same-named paths at the repository root, DELETING any the base checkpoint does not hold (Git.swift:619) and overwriting any it does (Git.swift:607-611). The revert sheet shows the mis-derived names, which read like plausible file names, and the revert reports success.
criteria_detail: C1: files at the repository root that the turn never touched are deleted outright at Git.swift:619, and uncommitted content in them is not recoverable from the repository.
C4: preview, restore and the app's own report all look normal, so the user gets no signal that the wrong files were acted on and the intended ones left alone.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly, including the data-loss path. Exact parity, including the defect.
Harden the path so the loss cannot occur. This is a recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of previewRestore path derivation
any revert path that deletes files not present in the base checkpoint
